content:
It is now the last two months of the Mathlib Initiative year 1 roadmap https://mathlib-initiative.org/roadmap/ . It is not clear to me whether it is still being followed or how much progress were made. I understand that a lot of things have changed over the past year, and a roadmap isn't set in stone; still, to an outsider it looks like deviation from some of objectives and milestones listed there. For example, I couldn't find quarterly reviews, and specifically for reports on review response time. Going with anecdotal data, it feels worse than last year.

What is Mathlib Initiative's plan on these objectives?

Thanks for asking! You're right that public quarterly reports on e.g. the review performance was in the roadmap; indeed, no such reports exist yet. I have passed this on to the right people at the MI, they are aware of this and are working on a report that's suitable for public sharing. (There are internal reports, but these contain some yet-confidential information, so cannot be shared unedited.)
There is also work underway on a roadmap for the second year, which will be published once it is complete.

I agree there is a review crisis, with latencies being higher than e.g. in January. (I'm not sure it's worse than last year; the situation felt markedly better e.g. September through January.) It's a complicated topic with many factors. I (personally) also wish I had easy answers! Some plans include better tooling to help reviewers, growing the pool of reviewers (the mathlib review bootcamp helped, hopefully there will be another edition next year) and surely many things I don't remember right now.
@Weiyi Wang I have posted a reflection on year 1 here: #general > Reflection: the first year of the Mathlib Initiative
Create tools for AI training data extraction and integration: what this task current status
This is answered in the reflection posted above. (If you have further questions after reading that, that thread is a good place to ask.)

I am doing to produce static data of entire Mathlib4 theorem with dependencies. The data cover 100% theorems without any dropping and data has been tested in standalone environment. From my research, I do not find any data set as same as my qualiy so I want to know exactly current status of that work to check my work is necessary to publish or not

Can you ask a more precise question? It's impossible to answer you right now. (For instance, there are many kinds of static data you could extract.) The above post, section D4, links to the datasets produced by the MI.
@Adam Topaz The hugging face datasets are all data sets the MI produces, right?
Question is: which tool to use to extract data from mathlib4, by elab/info tree , trace log or build new tool for this purpose
I don't understand your question. (And I don't see your message tries to elaborate on the question I put.)
From hugging face output result, it looks use dojo or trace log to produce data. It only has tactic dataset of theorem. So it might have limited theorems from mathlib4
There are three datasets on HuggingFace - not just one.

You're asking two different things: what tool is being used to produce this data? (The answer is: LeanScout, and it's in the post I linked above.) And secondly: does it include all theorems from mathlib? (The answer is yes.)

@Linfeng Song you can think of LeanScout as a harness for running data extractors. You define your own data extractor (here's an example) and lean scout handles things like writing the dataset to parquet shards.
Got it . It uses metaprogramming and similar as Jixia or other existing tool to use metaprogramming api
One more question: Is the data generated by LeanScout verified by the Lean engine after creation? If so, what is the verification process, and where can I find the testing or verification code?
